speaker: Unknown
en: I think Hollywood is going to be the last industry to adopt any of these things.
zh: 我认为好莱坞将是采用这些任何事物的最后一个行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea of doing full-length films, has that gone by the wayside as you found your market niche, or do you still imagine going that?
zh: 制作全长电影的想法，在你找到市场利基后已经被搁置了吗，还是你仍然想象去那个方向？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what you will see AI-generated entertainment is not in the cinemas, it's not on Netflix.
zh: 我想你会看到 AI 生成的娱乐内容不在电影院，也不在 Netflix 上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I kept asking, why don't you put an avatar on this that would engage students more?
zh: 我一直在问，为什么你不在这个上面放一个虚拟形象，那样能更多地吸引学生？

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is for K through 12, because students are bored by text on a screen.
zh: 这是针对 K 到 12 年级的，因为学生们对屏幕上的文字感到厌倦。

speaker: Unknown
en: They kept telling us the same thing.
zh: 他们一直告诉我们同样的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know I'm creating all this content and no one is reading it.
zh: 我知道我正在创作所有这些内容，但没人读它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And even if they do read it, they don't remember anything.
zh: 即使他们读了，他们也什么都记不住。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm wasting my time.
zh: 所以我在浪费时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: I need to create video and audio content.
zh: 我需要创作视频和音频内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for kids, if you could go, if you could personalize their education in two ways, interest-based and with a celebrity or a person that they know, it'd be amazing, right?
zh: 我认为对于孩子来说，如果你可以，如果你能通过两种方式个性化他们的教育，基于兴趣的，以及用一个名人或者他们认识的人，那将会很棒，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Hey, Victor, it's great to meet you.
zh: 嘿，Victor，很高兴见到你。

speaker: Unknown
en: As I mentioned a moment ago, I was an early Synthesia.
zh: 就我刚才提到的，我是个早期的 Synthesia。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have trouble pronouncing the company name and have used it for years.
zh: 我发音这家公司名字有困难，并且已经使用它好几年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'd like you to start by introducing yourself to listeners, give your background so far as it's relevant, and the story of how you came to start the company.
zh: 但我想请你先向听众介绍一下你自己，给出你的背景只要它是相关的，以及你是如何开始创办这家公司的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, sure.
zh: 好的，当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm Victor, and I'm one of the co-founders and the CEO of Synthesia today.
zh: 所以我是 Victor，我是联合创始人之一，也是今天 Synthesia 的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I grew up in Copenhagen in Denmark, and I think my path to a world-famous company started in my early childhood years.
zh: 我在丹麦的哥本哈根长大，我认为我通向一家世界著名公司的道路始于我童年的早期。

speaker: Unknown
en: I loved reading, I loved computers.
zh: 我热爱阅读，我热爱计算机。

speaker: Unknown
en: In my late teenage years, I figured out I could make some money off my interest in computers, so I began making websites for local businesses, e-commerce stores, kind of small projects like that where I could make pretty good money for a 17-year-old.
zh: 在我十几岁后期，我弄明白我可以利用我对计算机的兴趣赚点钱，所以我开始为当地企业制作网站，电子商务商店，诸如此类的小项目，在那里作为一个17岁的我可以赚相当不错的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was pretty good at it.
zh: 我很擅长这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: Started running their marketing and kind of did it for some years, but eventually kind of capped out in how intellectually interesting it could be to help my local tennis store sell more tennis rackets.
zh: 开始负责他们的市场营销，做了几年，但最终在帮助我的本地网球商店卖更多网球拍在思维上能有多有趣这一点上碰到了天花板。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I went to the Danish startup ecosystem.
zh: 所以我进入了丹麦的创业生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was there for three years, found myself in like product and growth roles.
zh: 我在那里待了三年，发现自己处于产品和增长的角色中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I have a bachelor in computer science and business, but honestly, I was never really there.
zh: 我有计算机科学和商业的学士学位，但老实说，我从未真正在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was more interested in building companies.
zh: 我对建立公司更感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: After having worked in the Danish ecosystem for some years, I knew I wanted to build my own company.
zh: 在丹麦生态系统工作几年后，我知道我想建立自己的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I also knew that I wasn't super interested in building accounting tools and bookkeeping tools and like normal business process stuff.
zh: 我也知道我对构建会计工具和簿记工具以及像正常的商业流程那些东西不是超级感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've always loved science fiction.
zh: 我一直热爱科幻小说。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love French ideas.
zh: 我热爱法国的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love the weird, wonderful corners of the internet and what's happening in the world.
zh: 我热爱互联网上奇异的、美妙的角落以及世界上正在发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I wanted to combine my interest in building products with that.
zh: 我想把我对构建产品的兴趣与那结合起来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I moved to London.
zh: 所以我搬到了伦敦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I spent a year figuring out what company I wanted to build.
zh: 我花了一年时间弄清楚我想建立什么样的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Met a guy called Matthias Lister, who was an associate professor at Stanford at the time.
zh: 遇到了一个叫 Matthias Lister 的人，他是斯坦福大学当时的副教授。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he'd done a research paper called Face to Face, which is sort of the first research paper demonstrating a neural network producing, you know, very photorealistic video.
zh: 他做过一篇叫《面对面》的研究论文，这是第一篇展示神经网络生成，你知道，非常逼真的视频的研究论文。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we look back at it today, it's less impressive.
zh: 当我们今天回顾它时，它没那么令人印象深刻。

speaker: Unknown
en: The world has moved on quite a lot, but I saw this and I felt like there's something very magical about it.
zh: 世界已经发展了很多，但我看到了这个，我觉得它有一些非常神奇的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And as someone who loves creative things in my spare time, you know, I make music, dabbled in like Photoshop and a bit of video editing, 3D rendering.
zh: 作为一个在业余时间热爱创造性事物的人，你知道，我制作音乐，涉猎过 Photoshop 和一点视频编辑、3D 渲染。

speaker: Unknown
en: I saw the technology, I was like, this is going to change everything we know about how we create video and media in general, and also how we consume it eventually.
zh: 我看到了这项技术，我想，这将改变我们所知道的关于我们如何创建视频和媒体的所有事情，以及最终我们如何消费它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I decided to start a company around it, which took a while to convince Matthias.
zh: 所以我决定围绕它创办一家公司，这花了一段时间来说服 Matthias。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was 25 years old at the time.
zh: 我当时25岁。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think he thought I was, you know, he wasn't very interested in the beginning.
zh: 我认为他觉得我，你知道，他在开始并不是很感兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: But with enough persistence, we kind of got there in the end.
zh: 但凭着足够的坚持，我们最终做到了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we ended up founding a company based on basically two big ideas.
zh: 我们最终基于基本上两个大想法创立了一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first one being that AI is increasingly going to be able to generate content, not just analyze patterns and data.
zh: 第一个是 AI 将越来越多地能够生成内容，而不仅仅是分析模式和数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's going to change the equation around how we create content, right?
zh: 这将改变我们如何创建内容的等式，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to drive the marginal cost of creating content to zero.
zh: 它将把创建内容的边际成本驱动到零。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the cost in dollars of creating content is going to be very low.
zh: 所以以美元计算的创建内容的成本将会非常低。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cost in time is going to be very low.
zh: 时间的成本将会非常低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the time and skill required to create video is going to be very low.
zh: 创作视频所需的时间和技能将会非常低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's the bits up until now.
zh: 我认为这就是到目前为止的这些片段。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's the market right now where anyone can go on the internet, they can prompt something in a few minutes and they can produce something that's very, very high quality.
zh: 我认为这就是目前的市场，任何人都可以上网，在几分钟内提示一些东西，他们就能产出非常非常高质量的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that changes like the...
zh: 这改变了像是……

speaker: Unknown
en: The nature of video production, right?
zh: 视频制作的本质，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: When you reached out to him, first of all, how did you happen to read the paper?
zh: 当你联系他的时候，首先，你是怎么读到那篇论文的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because this is an experience I think anyone who follows archive, you know, the repository of preprint papers has experienced.
zh: 因为这是一种我认为任何关注档案馆，也就是预印本论文库的人，都经历过的体验。

speaker: Unknown
en: You see these great ideas.
zh: 你看到了这些很棒的想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: You think, wow, you could build a company around that.
zh: 你会想，哇，你可以以此建立一家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of times that research just fades into the woodwork.
zh: 很多时候那种研究就这样淡出了视野。

speaker: Unknown
en: How did you happen to read the paper and how did you reach out to him?
zh: 你是怎么读到那篇论文的，又是怎么联系他的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So when I moved to London in 2016, VR and AR was like the hype cycle at the time.
zh: 所以当我在 2016 年搬到伦敦时，VR 和 AR 就像是当时的炒作周期。

speaker: Unknown
en: The Oculus headset just came out and I was very enthralled by all this tech and I actually thought I was going to start a VR company.
zh: Oculus 头显刚刚推出，我被所有这些技术迷住了，我实际上以为我要开一家 VR 公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I spent a lot of time just like meeting researchers, meeting companies.
zh: 所以我花了很多时间就像会见研究人员，会见公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: I worked as kind of like a freelance consultant to some big companies and what they should do with VR and AR.
zh: 我作为某种自由职业顾问为一些大公司工作，咨询他们应该用 VR 和 AR 做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I kind of pretty quickly came to the conclusion that outside of the headset being very clunky as a barrier for VR adoption, the other thing that was a big problem was that creating content for VR is very expensive, you know?
zh: 我某种程度上相当快地得出了一个结论，除了头显非常笨重作为 VR 采用的障碍之外，另一件大事是，为 VR 创作内容是非常昂贵的，你知道吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because basically what you're doing is you're building a computer game.
zh: 因为基本上你正在做的是你在构建一个电脑游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that comes at a very high cost, even compared to video production.
zh: 而且这成本非常高，即使是跟视频制作相比。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I kind of started to have this interest in how can we make content creation easier?
zh: 所以我开始有了这种兴趣，我们如何能让内容创作更容易？

speaker: Unknown
en: That took me down a path of things like volumetric capture, which is you have like a lot of cameras in an array around you.
zh: 这让我走上了一条像体积捕获这样的道路，也就是你周围有一阵列的很多摄像机。

speaker: Unknown
en: You go in and you do a performance and you get a 3D asset out of that.
zh: 你进去，表演一下，然后你就能得到一个 3D 资产。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could port into VR.
zh: 你可以移植到 VR 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was interesting.
zh: 那很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: I was part of setting up a studio for this in London.
zh: 我是参与在伦敦为此建立工作室的一员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a whole bunch of other interesting ideas of like how content creation could be made easier.
zh: 还有一大堆其他关于如何让内容创作变得更容易的有趣想法。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I was following that space and Matthias Diesner had a lot of papers in this space around VR, but he also had this paper coming out called Face to Face.
zh: 所以我关注那个领域，Matthias Diesner 在这个关于 VR 的领域有很多论文，但他还有这篇即将发表的论文叫 Face to Face。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I saw that, I just think I had this eureka moment where, you know, instead of trying to do this with VR, where we're both trying to bring a new type of media to market, which is hard and a clunky headset, and we're trying to make it easier to create content, that's kind of a double whammy of very hard problems.
zh: 当我看到那个时，我想我有了这个灵光一现的时刻，你知道，与其试图用 VR 做这个，我们要么都在试图将一种新型媒体推向市场，这很难而且头显笨重，而且我们要试图让内容创作更容易，这就像是双重打击的非常难的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: If this works with video,
zh: 如果这对视频有效，

speaker: Unknown
en: That's interesting, right?
zh: 那很有趣，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: Because video, the infrastructure of video is already in place.
zh: 因为视频，视频的基础设施已经到位了。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're all spending time on YouTube.
zh: 我们都在 YouTube 上花时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like video is, you know, you could just take an AI video and replace it with a normal video.
zh: 就像视频是，你知道，你可以直接拿一个 AI 视频并用一个普通视频替换它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the distribution problem wasn't really there.
zh: 所以分发问题并不真正存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's where I kind of started to feel like this is actually like a very interesting business idea because if we can solve this for video, we, you know, we can, we can distribute to the world pretty quickly.
zh: 我想这就是我开始觉得这实际上是一个非常有意思的商业点子的地方，因为如果我们能为视频解决这个问题，我们，你知道，我们可以，我们可以很快地分发到世界各地。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you started the company then and that's very funny I was about the VR stuff I was running the New York Times operations in China at the time and when VR first came out and there was a company I'm sure they've long disappeared that came through town and they
zh: 所以你就那时创办了公司，这很有趣，关于 VR 的东西，我当时负责《纽约时报》在中国的业务，当 VR 刚出来的时候，有一家公司我肯定他们早就消失了，来到这个城市，他们……

speaker: Unknown
en: They were showing us their cameras.
zh: 他们在向我们展示他们的摄像机。

speaker: Unknown
en: I got very excited, and I ended up partnering with Chinese media to do a big conference on VR.
zh: 我很兴奋，我最后与中国媒体合作举办了一个关于 VR 的大型会议。

speaker: Unknown
en: I thought, boy, that's the future.
zh: 我想，天哪，那就是未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: But as it turns out, it wasn't.
zh: 但事实证明，它并不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when did you start Synthesia?
zh: 所以你是什么时候创立 Synthesia 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: And tell me about the name.
zh: 跟我讲讲这个名字。

speaker: Unknown
en: I always want to say Anesthesia.
zh: 我总想说 Anesthesia。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we started the company in 2017, but there was a lead up to that of, you know, trying to build a prototype and, you know, get the thesis down and all that, trying to raise money, which was very, very, very difficult because this was a very non-consensus bet at the time.
zh: 所以我们在 2017 年创办了公司，但在此之前有一些铺垫，你知道，试图构建原型，你知道，把论点定下来，以及所有这些，试图融资，这非常非常非常困难，因为这在当时是一个非常非共识的赌注。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were basically telling people in 10 years, you can make a Hollywood film with nothing else but your imagination.
zh: 我们基本上是在告诉人们，在 10 年内，你可以仅凭你的想象力制作一部好莱坞电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: And at that point in time, like that was certainly like a sci-fi dream more than it was something that was like tangible to investors.
zh: 在那个时候，这当然更像是一个科幻梦，而不是某种对投资者来说是触手可及的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And every investor just wanted to invest in fintech at the time.
zh: 而且每个投资者那时只想投资金融科技。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in October 2017, we raised the first funding round, got a million dollars from Mark Cuban, who was a big believer and has been since day one.
zh: 但在 2017 年 10 月，我们筹集了第一轮融资，从 Mark Cuban 那里拿到了一百万美元，他是一个坚定的信徒，从第一天起就是。

speaker: Unknown
en: That process.
zh: 那个过程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how did you get to Mark Cuban?
zh: 那么你是怎么联系到 Mark Cuban 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Just a cold outreach?
zh: 只是冷接触吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had a long list of investors that we tried to speak to and we weren't very lucky.
zh: 所以我们有一长份我们尝试去交谈的投资人名单，而且我们不是很幸运。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we had a list over like...
zh: 而且我们要一份大约像……

speaker: Unknown
en: Business angels, wealthy people that fit well in the kind of media and technology Venn diagram, and Mark was one of them.
zh: 商业天使，那种很符合媒体和技术韦恩图的富豪，Mark 就是其中之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we found his email online actually by downloading a hack.
zh: 所以我们实际上通过在网上下载一个黑客攻击找到了他的邮箱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It only got hacked a few years prior, and there was a lot of emails in that hack.
zh: 它只在几年前被黑过，那个黑客攻击里有很多邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: We found his email, we sent him a cold email, and he responded back within four minutes saying, I think this is really interesting, came back with some more questions, and then we had a 14-hour email conversation with him.
zh: 我们找到了他的邮箱，给他发了一封冷邮件，他在四分钟内回复说，我觉得这真的很有趣，带回了一些更多的问题，然后我们进行了一次 14 小时的邮件往来。

speaker: Unknown
en: Mark doesn't do any video calls or normal calls.
zh: Mark 不做任何视频通话或普通通话。

speaker: Unknown
en: He only does email.
zh: 他只用邮件。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so 14 hours later, he'd asked a lot of great questions.
zh: 所以 14 小时后，他问了很多很好的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he said, I'll do a million dollars if the diligence checks out.
zh: 他说，我会投一百万美元，如果尽职调查通过的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one thing that was very interesting about this process was Mark was aware of the research paper.
zh: 我觉得关于这个过程有一件很有趣的事是 Mark 知道那篇研究论文。

speaker: Unknown
en: He had implemented it himself at home.
zh: 他自己在家实现了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And he 100% believed in the vision around you're going to be able to make a Hollywood film from your laptop antenna.
zh: 并且他 100% 相信那个愿景，关于你将能够从你的笔记本电脑天线制作好莱坞电影。

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have to discuss that.
zh: 我们不需要讨论那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: He was just interested in how are you going to build a company around it?
zh: 他只是感兴趣你要如何围绕它建立一家公司？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are you going to do until the technology actually works?
zh: 以及在技术真正生效之前你要做什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Which is a very different conversation than every other investor we spoke to, where we had to start at like, hey, this thing's going to be possible in 10 years.
zh: 这是一个与我们交谈过的其他所有投资人非常不同的对话，对于那些人我们不得不从像，嘿，这东西将在 10 年后成为可能开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they just, if they didn't, you know, Mark shared the same belief around us.
zh: 而他们只是，如果他们没有，你知道，Mark 分享了同样的关于我们的信念。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he was evaluating us as a team, whereas everyone else, we had to try and convince them about this like worldview.
zh: 所以他是在把我们作为一个团队来评估，而其他人，我们必须尝试说服他们关于这种像世界观的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's very hard.
zh: 而且那很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we got turned down by, I think almost a hundred investors before Mark actually invested.
zh: 所以我们被拒绝了，我想在 Mark 实际投资之前有接近一百个投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that became the, yeah, the premise of the company.
zh: 而那成为了，是的，这家公司的前提。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
